facts.text: When the Santa Fe Railroad laid tracks a mile from town in 1887, San Marcos residents moved the community closer in 1903 to stay near the rail line.
Founded in 1983, the San Marcos Historical Society and Museum preserves Native American, Spanish colonial, and agricultural heritage while offering an extensive library of local history.
The Calaboose African American Museum, open Wednesdays through Saturdays, displays exhibits on Buffalo Soldiers, Tuskegee Airmen, WWII, Civil Rights, and the Ku Klux Klan.
Eddie Durham, born in San Marcos in 1906, is celebrated with a park, jazz celebration, and tribute events honoring his pioneering electric guitar work.
An illuminated cross atop a hill above Lake San Marcos has served as a nighttime landmark visible from many parts of the city for decades.
A giant letter “P” for Palomar on the hillside above San Marcos State University is a landmark visible miles away, showcasing the campus’s presence.
